text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 2.8% today, bouncing back from a sharp 6.4% drop on October 27th. The rebound appears tied to ongoing geopolitical tensions—Qatari mediators held talks in Tehran on Friday aimed at restarting U.S.-Iran negotiations, which reduces the immediate risk of escalating conflict in the Middle East. Since oil prices and refining margins typically rise when geopolitical risk spikes, any sign of de-escalation or diplomatic progress can initially pull prices back down, then stabilize them as investors assess the new baseline.

The company also announced a leadership change and update on October 29th, the same day CNBC flagged that Big Oil earnings guidance could matter more than headline numbers—suggesting investors are parsing management commentary closely. The stock remains down 6% over two weeks despite refineries running at 92.8% capacity and fuel inventories remaining relatively tight, indicating the market is currently more cautious about the sector's near-term outlook than the refining fundamentals alone would suggest.
